title: Similarities and differences
keyIdea: People can be the same in some ways and different in others, all at once. Best friends can both like to paint and still have different hair, pets or languages. Families are made in lots of ways, and they are all families. When someone does a thing in a different way, it is not weird or wrong: ask about it and learn something new.

kid: Mia and Sam are best friends. They are both 6. They both like to paint. That is the same.
Mia has curly hair. Sam has straight hair. At home Mia speaks Polish, and Sam speaks English. That is different.
Homes are not all the same. Kit lives with her two mums. Ravi lives with his gran. Leo lives with his dad and his big sister. They are all families.
Jun eats with chopsticks. That is not weird. It is a new thing to learn. Say, "Can you show me how?"
adult: This sits in personal, social and health education and in the DfE Relationships Education guidance for primary schools. Pupils learn that other families may look different from their own, and that they should respect those differences. They also learn to respect others who are very different from them, for example in looks, character or background. In the early years it links to the Early Learning Goal for People, Culture and Communities.

The key words are similarity, difference, respect, family, culture, language and celebration. A Venn diagram is a good tool at this age. It has two circles that cross, with the shared things in the middle. It shows a child that two people can share some things and differ in others at the same time.

Common mistakes: thinking a best friend must be the same in every way, or that someone who looks different shares nothing with you. Another slip is to call a different way of eating, dressing or speaking weird or wrong, or to think a real family needs a mum and a dad. Be careful not to ignore differences either; name them kindly and with interest.

In the lab your child sorts six facts about two friends into same or different, drags facts into a Venn diagram, builds three different families in a house, chooses a kind and curious reply to three differences, and finds what Diwali, Eid, Christmas and Lunar New Year all share.

familyTip: Draw two big crossing circles, one for you and one for your child. Put things only you like on your side, things only they like on theirs, and things you both like in the middle. Talk about how you are the same and different.

visual.caption: Kind or unkind about a difference? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort same and different, drag facts into a Venn diagram, build three families, choose kind replies and find what four special days share.

practice.prompt: Mia has curly hair. Sam has straight hair. Is that the same or different?
practice.hint: Is curly hair the same as straight hair?
practice.explain: Curly and straight are not the same, so that is a difference.

practice.prompt: Mia and Sam write down {n} things they both like. How many things go in the middle of the Venn diagram?
practice.hint: The middle is for things they both like.
practice.explain: Things they both like go in the middle, so {n} things go there.

practice.prompt: Kit lives with her two mums. Is that a family?
practice.hint: Do the people in Kit's home love and care for her?
practice.explain: Families are made in lots of ways. Kit and her two mums are a family.

practice.prompt: In a class, {a} children speak English at home and {b} speak another language at home. How many children are in the class?
practice.explain: {a} add {b} is {=a+b}. Lots of children speak more than one language.

pool.prompt: Ben uses a wheelchair. Tom does not. What could be the same about them?
choices: They are the same in every way
pool.hint: People who look different can still like the same things.
pool.explain: Ben and Tom can both like football. Being different in one way does not stop you sharing other things.

pool.prompt: Zofia says "Cześć!" It means hello in Polish. What is a kind thing to say?
pool.hint: Which one is kind and wants to find out more?
pool.explain: Asking to learn more is kind and curious. Polish is normal for Zofia.

pool.prompt: Mia and Sam both like to paint. Where does "Likes to paint" go in their Venn diagram?
pool.hint: Where do the two circles cross?
pool.explain: Things both of them like go in the middle, where the circles cross.

pool.prompt: Leo lives with his dad and {s} sisters. How many people live in Leo's home, with Leo too?
pool.hint: Count Leo, his dad and each sister.
pool.explain: Leo, his dad and {s} sisters make {=s+2} people. That is Leo's family.

pool.prompt: Jun eats with chopsticks. What is true?
choices: It is a different way to eat
It is the wrong way to eat
pool.hint: Is there only one right way to eat?
pool.explain: Chopsticks are just a different way to eat. Lots of people use them every day.

pool.prompt: What do Diwali and Christmas both have?
pool.hint: Which one is on both days?
pool.explain: Both have special food with family and friends. A tree is for Christmas, and clay lamps are for Diwali.

pool.prompt: Mia and Sam list {t} things about themselves. {s} of them are the same. How many are different?
pool.hint: Take the same ones away from the whole list.
pool.explain: {t} take away {s} is {=t-s} things that are different.

pool.prompt: Amira wears a hijab. You want to play tag. What do you say?
pool.hint: Can Amira play in her hijab?
pool.explain: Amira can play just as she is. Ask her to play.
